(basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 1,402 (2.5 apg) }} '''Reggie Williams''' (born March 5, 1964) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played ten seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] college player at [[Georgetown University]] and was a member of their [[1983–84 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1983–84 National Championship team]]. ==Early life and college== Williams began his career as a [[McDonald's High School All-American]] while attending [[Paul Laurence Dunbar High School (Baltimore, Maryland)|Paul Laurence Dunbar High School]] in Baltimore, where he played with fellow NBA players [[Muggsy Bogues]], [[Reggie Lewis]], and [[David Wingate (basketball)|David Wingate]]. The 1981–82 Dunbar Poets finished the season at 29–0 during Williams's junior season and finished 31–0 during his senior season, and were ranked first in the nation by USA Today.{{cite web|url=http://slamonline.com/online/high-school/2007/09/dunbar-high-brick-house/|title=Dunbar High: Brick House|publisher=SLAM Online|date=September 21, 2007|access-date=December 9, 2008}} He then attended [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and enjoyed an outstanding collegiate career. In his four seasons at Georgetown, he was amongst career leaders in scoring, rebounding, assists and steals in school history, finishing no lower than seventh in any category. As a freshman, he scored 19 points and grabbed seven rebounds against the [[University of Houston]] in the 1984 national championship game which the Hoyas won 84–75. Williams was named Most Valuable Player of the championship game. As a senior during the 1986–87 season, Williams was the leader of a young team which became a contender for a national championship. During that season he led the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] in scoring, and led the team in rebounding, steals and blocked shots, and was third in assists. Because of Williams's play, it led Georgetown coach Thompson to dub the team "Reggie and the Miracles".{{cite news| url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9B0DEFDD1031F931A35750C0A961948260&sec=&spon=&pagewanted=2 | work=The New York Times | title=The Big East Tournament; Williams Is Going Out In Style | first=Roy S. | last=Johnson | date=March 2, 1987 | access-date=May 22, 2010}} The team won a share of the 1986–87 Big East Championship and the Big East Tournament. In the 1987 NCAA tournament, the Hoyas reached the Southeast Regional Final, but lost to [[Providence College]], 88–73. ==Professional career== Williams was selected with the fourth pick overall of the [[1987 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. On December 12, 1987, Williams scored 34 points and grabbed eight rebounds in a loss against the [[Seattle SuperSonics]].{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/198712120SEA.html| title = Los Angeles Clippers at Seattle SuperSonics Box Score, December 12, 1987 {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}} Williams would spend ten seasons (1987–1997) in the league, playing for the Clippers, [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[San Antonio Spurs]], [[Denver Nuggets]] (who he spent parts of 6 seasons with, the most of any franchise he played with), [[Indiana Pacers]] and [[New Jersey Nets]]. During the [[1991-92 NBA season]] with Denver, Williams played 81 games and averaged career-highs of 18.2 points and 1.8 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willire01.html|title=Reggie Williams NBA Stats|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|accessdate=30 June 2026}} Twice in that season Williams recorded a career-best 7 steals in a single game.[https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/reggie-williams-career-high-steals Reggie Williams Career High 7 Steal Games] On December 1, 1992, Williams scored 35 points and grabbed 9 rebounds in a 112–105 win against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/199212010DEN.html| title = Houston Rockets at Denver Nuggets Box Score, December 1, 1992 {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}} In the [[1994 NBA playoffs]], Williams played a key role in Denver's unprecedented upset of the SuperSonics in the first round. It was the first time in league history that an 8 seed beat a 1 seed in the first round.{{Cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/1994/05/08/no-8-denver-nuggets-upsets-no-1-seed-seattle-supersonics/|title = Stunning! No. 8 Denver Nuggets' overtime win upsets No. 1 seed Seattle SuperSonics|date = May 8, 1994}} He retired with career totals of 7,508 points and 2,393 rebounds. In July 2021, sportswriter [[Bill Simmons]] said “I still feel like if Reggie Williams goes to a different team, his entire career is different. The Clippers stamp went right on him,” when discussing the [[1987 NBA draft]].{{Cite web|url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=EY-_mzxTQTc|title = How Does Giannis Compare to Hakeem? | the Bill Simmons Podcast|website = [[YouTube]]}} ==Life after the NBA== Williams became the boys' [[coach (basketball)|basketball coach]] at [[Towson Catholic High School]] on May 30, 2009. He had previously served in the same capacity at Jericho Christian Academy in [[Landover, Maryland]] until it closed several weeks later.[http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/highschool/bal-va.williams31may31,0,2196387.story Barker, Jeff. "Towson Catholic hires Dunbar great as new coach," ''The Baltimore Sun'', Sunday, May 31, 2009.]{{dead link|date=August 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In 2010, he became coach at [[Archbishop Carroll High School (Washington, D.C.)|Archbishop Carroll High School]] in [[Washington, D.C.]][http://www.casualhoya.com/2010/5/17/1476200/georgetown-great-reggie-williams Georgetown Great Reggie Williams Hired by Carroll] He resigned in February 2013.{{cite news| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/highschools/reggie-williams-resigns-as-carroll-basketball-coach-after-clashing-with-team-parents-school-principal/2013/02/08/f595aaf4-7224-11e2-8b8d-e0b59a1b8e2a_story.html | newspaper=The Washington Post | title=Reggie Williams resigns as Carroll basketball coach after clashing with team parents, school principal | first=Brandon | last=Parker | date=February 8, 2013 | access-date=January 1, 2014}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===NBA=== Source ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|1987}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[1987–88 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
